- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.3) or flat (0.0), model often overshoots downward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid premature bottoming.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model frequently overreacts with exaggerated continuation; cap forecast increase to 3–5% max from peak.
- If 3+ consecutive days of low sentiment (0.0 or negative), model underreacts to mean reversion; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to counteract downward drift.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture short-term mean reversion; apply a 1–2% downward adjustment if recent 7-day average is above 30-day average.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead for bullish sentiment, delay 1–2 days for bearish.
